seo_description: Free, open-source menu bar app that plays a chime and shows a banner when your Mac battery hits the low or full level you set. Native, no network access.
hero_sub: ChargeLevelChime lives in your menu bar and plays a sound and posts a banner when your battery reaches the low or full level you chose. Defaults are 20% and 80%.
features_sub: Set your own limits, pick your own sounds, and stay quiet when you need to.

features.title: Low and full thresholds
features.desc: Set the low and high levels with sliders right in the menu bar dropdown, or with steppers in Settings. The two are always kept at least 5% apart.

features.title: Chime plus a visible banner
features.desc: Each alert plays a sound and posts a plug-in or unplug banner. An optional critical alert at 5% plays three times and is delivered as Time Sensitive.

features.title: Your choice of sounds
features.desc: Pick a separate sound for low, charged and critical alerts from your system sounds, preview it, or choose your own audio file.

features.title: Repeats, quiet hours, snooze
features.desc: Repeat once or every 1 to 30 minutes until resolved. Quiet hours mute sounds but keep banners, and you can snooze for 30 minutes from the menu.

features.title: Live status at a glance
features.desc: The menu bar shows a battery state icon, an optional percentage and a colored dot. The dropdown adds power source and time remaining when macOS provides it.

features.title: No startup blast, no network
features.desc: Alerts are held for 90 seconds after launch and re-arm with 2% hysteresis, so you are not spammed. It uses only Apple frameworks and makes no network calls.

permissions_step: Allow notifications when macOS asks on first launch, so battery banners can appear; sounds still play if you decline.

faq.q: Is ChargeLevelChime really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. There are no ads, accounts or in-app purchases, and an optional Support button links to Ko-fi.

Only notifications, requested on first launch so banners can be shown. Launch at login and file access for a custom sound are optional. It does not ask for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Microphone, Location or network access.
Your settings are stored locally in the standard macOS preferences for the app. Nothing is sent anywhere, since the app has no network calls or analytics.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source.
